Very good question tiger.

Mainly 2 things made the change for me

1] Simplify the levels of interest analysis: meaning stick to one or two types of structures to define levels

2] take the most extreme levels of HTF ( H4 and up). with HTF reaction always provide some pips, to allow you lock into profit as quick, even if the trade do not turn to be a swing.

The structures I use most is Quasimodo.

author: benhur
text:
sylntthunder

Yes you are absolutely on track with the HTF reasoning.

The confirmation for the Weekly level to short, was the LTF Can Can / QM price action.

I think we both have similar analysis, I care mostly about LTF confirmation of HTF levels.

I dont think there is such thing of over trading, your enthusiasm for this profession will win eventually, and you will be benefited with the best job on earth only few can do.

My break was when I started trading HTF levels with LTF confirmation. taking only most extreme levels has so many advantages.

1. first your risk is very low, and so the time it take for conviction of the trade success potential.

2. with the extremes, most of the time you have the privileged to profit from minor reactions. so your winning and gain experience is much greater.

3. at the extremes your psychology state is very comfortable. you dont sweat while trading, and you learn to just hate any minor drawdown.

Hope it helps a little

Keep on the trading enthusiasm.

G

author: benhur
text:
I got this question in private message, I think it is better to reply it in public as I get similar questions:Hi Benhur,

first, a very big thanks to your generous sharing of your charts and insights in the forum - your posts have been a real inspiration and eye-opener to a fledging trader like me.

In particular, I think how you approach the market really makes sense - especially the part on LTF confirmation of HTF levels. If you don't mind, I have 2 questions:

1. You mentioned that the levels structure you use most is the QM. Does that mean that you start your analysis by looking for QM levels at significant H4/D1 swing highs or swing lows (which I assume are the extremes)?

2. As for LTF confirmation, are you referring to the LTF structure at the source of the HTF level or LTF entry set-up? Looking at your charts, you based your entry on some LTF entry set-ups when the price returns to the level, but do you also look at the LTF at the source of the HTF level to pinpoint the exact level?

Basically I am scanning for QM levels of HTF. If the level itself is at extreme, I would be more comfortable to take it as is.

There are more QM levels at Mid way of HTF - those offer scalp opportunities.

LTF confirmation would be a newly forming QM structure occurring at logical HTF level and which is also explainable with LTF level at the origin of the HTF level i apply. LTF analysis of the origin provides the necessary resolution for better accuracy. TF are just price wrapped in arbitrary time period, while price is has a definite targets regardless of TF. Therefore MTF analysis is so much important for our work.
